target_customer: Consumer product brands that want to test designs before manufacturing
problem: Brands guess which product designs will sell and end up with surplus inventory. Crowdery let brands run design votes on their sites and take pre-orders on the winning design.
business_model: Percentage of pre-order sales from brand-run design voting contests
product_category: Design voting and pre-order tool for e-commerce brands

founders.name: Maran Nelson
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by YC page and TechCrunch (2013-08-15). Later CEO of Clara Labs per search results.

founders.name: Aditya Viswanathan
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by YC page and TechCrunch. No background in opened sources.

competitors.name: Fab.com
competitors.what: Design focused flash sale and shopping discovery site
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a discovery site that Crowdery's planned marketplace resembled

technical_complexity.rationale: An embeddable voting widget plus pre-order checkout and a brand dashboard. Standard web engineering for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Brand partnerships (150 reported in 2013) and vote data gave some value, but the widget and contest format were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying the tool. The founders moved to a different product in 2014 instead.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported 150 brand partners and an average 15 percent of page visitors completing the vote form, which suggests brand interest in pre-launch demand testing.

rebrands.why: YC page header says the company is now Clara (YC S14, claralabs.com). A reason was not found.

brand_strength.rationale: A short crowd plus ery coinage with some launch press, but the name was dropped within a year when the team moved to Clara, and no brand assets were found.

pivots.from: Crowdery design voting and pre-order tool
pivots.to: Clara, an email scheduling assistant (Clara Labs)
pivots.why: Reason not found. YC page notes the company is now Clara, YC S14.

outcome_analysis: Crowdery launched in August 2013 with about 150 brand partners but the design voting product was set aside when the founders became Clara, an email scheduling assistant that took funding from Sequoia in 2014 and a $7 million Series A in July 2017. The original product therefore ended through a pivot, and the cause beyond that is not public. The pivoted company was later reported by CB Insights as acquired in August 2019 with no acquirer named, so the long term result is unverified.
notes: crowdery.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched. Rounds listed are for the successor Clara Labs; one search result source says Clara was founded by Maran Nelson and Michael Akilian in 2014, so Clara may be a separate entity that took over the team. The 2014-09 Sequoia round was reported by TechCrunch as 'getting funding' with rumored $3 to 4 million, which is unverified, so amount is null. The August 2019 acquisition appears only on CB Insights, so exit type is unknown. Altss lists Crowdery as S13 while the YC page header mentions S14 for Clara.
